title.en: Prepare a common size Statement of Profit and Loss
Prepare a common size Balance Sheet

say.en: Of every 100 rupees a company earns, how much goes on materials, how much on staff, and how much is left as profit? A common size statement answers this at a glance. In this lesson: Prepare a common size Statement of Profit and Loss.
Prepare a common size Balance Sheet.
Interpret the percentages.

body.en: Each item is expressed as a percentage of a *common* base: revenue from operations for the Statement of Profit and Loss, and total assets (= total equity and liabilities) for the Balance Sheet. Columns: Particulars, Note No., Absolute amounts, Percentage of the base, often for two years side by side. It is a tool of vertical analysis.
body.kn: ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಗಾತ್ರದ ತಃಖ್ತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಲಾಭ ನಷ್ಟದ ತಃಖ್ತೆಗೆ ಕಾರ್ಯಾಚರಣಾ ಆದಾಯ ನೂರು, ಆಸ್ತಿ-ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿ ತಃಖ್ತೆಗೆ ಒಟ್ಟು ಆಸ್ತಿ ನೂರು.

problem.en: Revenue from operations ₹8,00,000; cost of materials consumed ₹4,80,000; employee benefits ₹80,000; other expenses ₹40,000; tax 30% of profit. Prepare a common size Statement of Profit and Loss.

steps.en: Revenue = 100%. Materials 4,80,000 ÷ 8,00,000 = 60%; employee benefits 10%; other expenses 5%.

answer.en: Out of every ₹100 of revenue, ₹17.50 is profit after tax.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Revenue from operations 8,00,000 rupees; cost of materials consumed 4,80,000 rupees; employee benefits 80,000 rupees; other expenses 40,000 rupees; tax 30 percent of profit. Prepare a common size Statement of Profit and Loss.
Revenue equals 100 percent. Materials 4,80,000 divided by 8,00,000 equals 60 percent; employee benefits 10 percent; other expenses 5 percent.
Total expenses 6,00,000 rupees equals 75 percent; profit before tax 2,00,000 rupees equals 25 percent.
Tax 60,000 rupees equals 7.5 percent; profit after tax 1,40,000 rupees equals 17.5 percent.
So the answer is Out of every 100 rupees of revenue, 17.50 rupees is profit after tax.

problem.en: Total assets ₹20,00,000: PPE ₹12,00,000; inventories ₹3,00,000; trade receivables ₹4,00,000; cash ₹1,00,000. Find the common size percentages.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Total assets 20,00,000 rupees: PPE 12,00,000 rupees; inventories 3,00,000 rupees; trade receivables 4,00,000 rupees; cash 1,00,000 rupees. Find the common size percentages.
PPE 12,00,000 divided by 20,00,000 equals 60 percent.
Inventories 15 percent; trade receivables 20 percent; cash 5 percent.
Check: 60 plus 15 plus 20 plus 5 equals 100 percent.
So the answer is 60 percent, 15 percent, 20 percent, 5 percent.

narration.en: Recap. Common size statements express items as % of a common base. Base: revenue from operations (P&L), total assets (Balance Sheet). It is vertical analysis and helps compare firms of different sizes.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಗಾತ್ರದ ತಃಖ್ತೆಗಳು ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಆಧಾರದ ಶೇಕಡಾವಾಗಿ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಆಧಾರ: ಕಾರ್ಯಾಚರಣಾ ಆದಾಯ (ಲಾಭ ನಷ್ಟ), ಒಟ್ಟು ಆಸ್ತಿ (ಆಸ್ತಿ-ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿ ತಃಖ್ತೆ). ಇದು ಲಂಬ ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆ; ಬೇರೆ ಗಾತ್ರದ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳನ್ನು ಹೋಲಿಸಲು ನೆರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Common size statements express items as % of a common base.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಗಾತ್ರದ ತಃಖ್ತೆಗಳು ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಆಧಾರದ ಶೇಕಡಾವಾಗಿ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: Base: revenue from operations (P&L), total assets Balance Sheet.
say.kn: ಆಧಾರ: ಕಾರ್ಯಾಚರಣಾ ಆದಾಯ (ಲಾಭ ನಷ್ಟ), ಒಟ್ಟು ಆಸ್ತಿ (ಆಸ್ತಿ-ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿ ತಃಖ್ತೆ).

say.en: It is vertical analysis and helps compare firms of different sizes.
